#6230. 17 Best Airbnbs in Bangkok for Your Next Trip to Thailand's Capital

A vast metropolis where modern skyscrapers mix with antique wooden houses, Bangkok is, in my opinion, one of the best cities in the world. Whether you’re on the hunt for boat noodles or Thai massages, there’s so much to do and no bad time of year to visit. And when it comes to where to stay, travelers will find just as much variety among the excellent lodging options. While this Thai city delivers a sensory overload of epic proportions, there are plenty of peaceful pockets and quiet corners perfect for catching your breath after a long day of exploring. One of the best ways to get a bit of solitude is by renting a dreamy Airbnb in the area.

Over the years, I’ve spent months in Thailand’s capital city. I've visited for weekend girls trips, concerts, and trips with family, staying everywhere from Siam to Chinatown. I've experienced the city's endless ways to fill your days, from world-class museums to addictive street food to some of Asia’s best cocktail bars. If you're planning a stay and want a little more elbow room than the city's hotels might allow, there are plenty of charming rentals to lay your head down at, from studios with incredible river views to massive homes for the whole family to shophouses in Chinatown. Read on for some of the best Airbnbs in Bangkok.

We've vetted these listings based on Superhost and Guest Favorite status, ratings, amenities, location, previous guest reviews, and decor.

Number of guests: 8Bed and bath: 4 bedrooms, 3 bathsWhy we love it: Spacious design, hot tub, screen projector

Baan Konja sits at the end of a cul-de-sac in the café-crazed neighborhood of Ekkamai. This stylish four-story home is an ideal launching pad for families or groups of friends looking for a peaceful stay. Guests will love how well laid out and spacious the setup is, with elegant tiled bathrooms, a rare private hot tub, four plush bedrooms (three kings and a room with two singles), and a comfy outdoor balcony area. According to past guests, the host, Michael, goes above and beyond to address any issues, including providing toothbrushes and slippers if you forget yours at home. He’s also able to suggest great cocktail spots.

Neighborhood: EkkamaiThings to do nearby: Wat That Thong Buddhist temple; top restaurants, cafés, and bars

Number of guests: 2Bed and bath: Studio, 1 bathWhy we love it: Incredible river and temple views, Thai design, trendy location

Ideal for couples and digital nomads, this large studio apartment is high up in a residential building surrounded by some of the city’s best spots for eating and drinking. Outfitted with a comfortable bed and couch next to a floor-to-ceiling window, it's designed with local touches like Thai art, colorful throw pillows, and a hand-carved wooden headboard. But travelers are really booking this room for the incredible views over the river and the nearby temple. Just outside, Michelin-star restaurants, riverside cafés, and trendy boutiques are steps away.

Neighborhood: Talat NoiThings to do nearby: Talat Noi street art, Chinatown, Wat Traimit Buddhist temple

Number of guests: 3Bed and bath: Studio, 1 bathWhy we love it: Beautiful design, large soaking tub, open-air spaces

The Clay Room is one of six short-term rental units in this newly renovated apartment building formerly owned by the host’s grandfather. This studio-style room is cozy with a comfortable bed and couch area, a large TV, and floor-to-ceiling glass-block windows. But to me, the best part of a stay here is the glass-block bathroom that looks like it could be out of a ’70s design magazine. Separated by a large velvet curtain, it has handcrafted clay-colored tiles, natural mineral paint, a huge soaking tub, and two curved glass-block partitions separating the toilet area and shower. There’s also an outdoor kitchen and a washer and dryer in the leafy backyard area.

Neighborhood: Thon BuriThings to do nearby: Wongwian Yai Park, IconSiam mall, Wat Arun Buddhist temple

Number of guests: 4Bed and bath: 2 bedrooms, 2 bathsWhy we love it: Quality craftsmanship, detailed design, first-floor spa

Located near the Jim Thompson House Museum, Chinatown, and Lumphini Park, this two-bedroom apartment is perfectly situated for exploring the best of Bangkok. Modern and stylish, its Scandinavian-style furniture is made with high-quality craftsmanship, according to past guests. The sleek style is accented with traditional pillows and throws woven with Thai patterns. Its main bedroom is huge with a king bed, while the second is smaller and has a set of bunk beds, making it ideal for a family with small children. When your feet get tired from exploring, walk down to the first-floor spa for a sublime Thai massage. (Of note, the apartment is on the second floor and there is not an elevator.)

Neighborhood: Hua LamphongThings to do nearby: Chinatown, Jim Thompson House Museum, Lumphini Park

Number of guests: 3Bed and bath: 1 bedroom, 1 bathWhy we love it: Central location, high ceilings, historic design

Steps from the Chao Phraya River, this 130-year-old heritage shophouse is in the pulsing heart of Bangkok. The city's best bars, cafés, shopping, and public transport are practically at your doorstep, but the Airbnb’s effortlessly cool design makes it hard to leave. Fun yellow and white checkered flooring, a coral-colored spiral staircase and matching ceiling, painted cement walls, and retro Thai art are a few of the standout elements of this cozy one-bedroom. Although the listing says it can accommodate up to five with a king-size bed and a sofa bed in the lofted bedroom, as well as a king-size sofa bed in the living area, guests say the house is compact, so I recommend it for couples or small families.

Neighborhood: Bang RakThings to do nearby: Sathorn Pier, IconSiam mall

Number of guests: 8Bed and bath: 3 bedrooms, 2 bathsWhy we love it: Private driveway with EV charging station, 60" smart TV, large kitchen

After years of working in European hotels, host Chureerut moved back to Bangkok to live with her mother and open her own Airbnb. Located between Bangkok’s two airports, slightly outside the city down a quiet alley, it’s a great setup for a peaceful family escape. Chureerut lovingly combines Scandinavian tiles and lighting with traditional Thai design elements, such as teak and rattan furniture. The two-bedroom house (a king and a queen) sleeps up to seven and is fully equipped with everything you could ever need, from a washer and dryer to a fully stocked kitchen and a dreamy outdoor patio with traditional Thai windows. Should you need any Bangkok recs, Chureerut and her mother are right next door.

Neighborhood: Khet Lat PhraoThings to do nearby: Central EastVille shopping center, Crystal Design Center

Number of guests: 2Bed and bath: 1 bedroom, 1 bathWhy we love it: Japanese-style design, pool, modern building

This full-service apartment on Bangkok's ​​Phahonyothin Road offers a quiet stay and easy access to the rest of the city. A seven-minute walk or a free tuk-tuk ride (provided by the building management) will take you to Sanampao Station, and from there, Bangkok is your fire-grilled oyster. The host has multiple one-bedroom apartments spread throughout the building, each with a subtle Japanese design: light timber, low beds (this one is a king), neutral tones, and large glass windows. Top-notch building amenities include a gym, outdoor swimming pool, and a massage parlor—a perfect tonic after a long flight.

Neighborhood: PhahonyothinThings to do nearby: Victory Monument, Jim Thompson House Museum

Number of guests: 4Bed and bath: 2 bedrooms, 1 bathWhy we love it: Stylish design, natural light, convenient location

This artfully curated apartment incorporates Scandi-chic touches throughout. Situated near Lumphini and Bechakitti Parks and just a short walk to the BTS, past guests have raved about the location. But its interiors are what really will catch your eye. The main living room has floor-to-ceiling windows with green views, rattan chairs, and a mustard-colored couch with colorful pillows. Find ocean-blue tiles in the kitchen for another fun pop of color. Its two king bedrooms have concrete floors, wooden furniture, and light pastel sheets. Black slate and white mosaic tiles adorn the bathroom, which includes a large tub. Keep in mind that it's located on the third floor and there is no elevator, so pack light!

Neighborhood: LumphiniThings to do nearby: Lumphini Park, One Bangkok, Benjakitti Park

Number of guests: 2Bed and bath: 2 bedrooms, 2 bathsWhy we love it: Outdoor bathroom, quiet workspace, tons of character

As soon as you check in here, you can tell it’s owned by an artist. Located in the historic center of Bangkok, chaotic Khaosan Road is a 10-minute walk away, but this two-bedroom renovated shophouse is a peaceful reprieve. Filled with fun art and an eclectic style, this cute and compact space includes a shared bedroom and living room, plus a second bed in a loft. Its large, exposed-brick dining room is ideal for a couple working remotely, and its outdoor bathroom is among the most unique I’ve seen in Bangkok.

Neighborhood: RattanakosinThings to do nearby: Khao San Road, The Grand Palace, Wat Pho temple, Loha Prasat “metal castle”

Number of guests: 2Bed and bath: 1 bedroom, 1 bathWhy we love it: Lush garden, badminton court, brushed concrete interiors

Tucked into a local area in Samrong on the far outskirts of Bangkok (accessible via the BTS SkyTrain), this one-bedroom Airbnb is perfect for travelers who want to escape the chaos—at least for a little while. The owners have outfitted their backyard guesthouse with cooling brushed concrete, vintage wooden doors, and comfortable bedding, including a contemporary pullout sectional. Reach out to the hosts for help arranging a badminton game at the nearby court, a market tour, or a few other neighborhood experiences. Plus, the fridge is stocked with drinks and snacks to enjoy while relaxing under a banana tree in the large garden.

Neighborhood: SamrongThings to do nearby: Pak Nam fish market, Talad Rot Fai Srinakarin night market, Bang Krachao man-made island

Number of guests: 5Bed and bath: 2 bedrooms, 1 bathWhy we love it: Great nearby food options, trendy tiles, access to hotel amenities

It’s all about coziness and convenience at this quaint two-bedroom (each with a queen) apartment near the SkyTrain and the Sathorn Central Pier. White walls, lofty ceilings, bamboo light fixtures, and handwoven wall tapestries make its newly renovated spaces feel airy and bright. Major brownie points go to the host, who can help with just about anything, including arranging an airport transfer, providing tips for the best local restaurants, and securing passes to use the neighboring hotel’s outdoor pool and fitness area (for a small daily fee).

Neighborhood: SilomThings to do nearby: Sathorn Pier, IconSiam mall

Number of guests: 4Bed and bath: 1 bedroom, 2 bathsWhy we love it: Sophisticated decor, powerful AC, designated workspace

Digital nomads flocking to Thailand—thanks to its visa—will love this fully-equipped house. During your stay here, you’ll find comfortable working areas, powerful AC, a stocked fridge, and even a printer. Located in a residential area outside the city center, the Ratchadaphisek MRT Station is just a five-minute walk away, connecting you to the city’s hotspots after office hours. Newly renovated, its trendy midcentury-modern decor is another stay highlight. Mismatched furniture, concrete floors, matte black fixtures, and pencil-strip bathroom tiles are all smart additions. It sleeps up to four with a queen in the bedroom and a sofa bed in the living room.

Neighborhood: RatchadaphisekThings to do nearby: Chatuchak Weekend Market, Jodd Fairs market

Number of guests: 6Bed and bath: 3 bedrooms, 2 bathsWhy we love it: Outdoor patio, eclectic design, tons of natural light

You'll find this delightfully eclectic three-bedroom respite on a quiet, tree-lined street in the residential Din Daeng area of Bangkok. Decorated with the owner’s paintings, parquet floors, and an eclectic blend of furniture, this homey abode is perfect for a young family or a group of friends. Its three bedrooms (two with kings, one with a queen) have unique styles, from wacky wallpaper to shiplap and fully tiled bathrooms. Each has a desk for working, but the peaceful patio with mango trees and ferns is a much better place to get the creative juices flowing.

Neighborhood: Din DaengThings to do nearby: Huai Khwang market, Ganesha Shrine, Thailand Cultural Center

Number of guests: 6Bed and bath: 2 bedrooms, 1 bathWhy we love it: Beautiful design, luxurious bathroom, fantastic location

As far as neighborhoods go, Bangkok’s Chinatown is hard to beat. The city’s best street food, hippest bars, and most vibrant shops are all steps from your door. Inside an ornate shophouse, this two-bedroom, one-bath home offers more modern finishes than its exterior implies. Its bathroom includes a high-tech rain shower, luxurious soaking tub, and cool Oxford encaustic tiles. The bedrooms here are huge, with chic black and rattan furniture, handwoven decoration, king beds, and large TVs. It’s ideal for families, friends, or two sets of couples. Note that the stairs here are steep, but all the creature comforts are worth it.

Neighborhood: ChinatownThings to do nearby: Chinatown, Wat Traimit temple, Talad Noi historic neighborhood

Number of guests: 4Bed and bath: 1 bedroom, 1 bathWhy we love it: Sweeping city views, Nordic design, soaking tub

Situated on the 36th floor of the famous State Tower (you may remember the building’s rooftop bar from The Hangover 2), the unbeatable city views are enough of a reason to book this high-rise. A trendy royal blue kitchen, tropical wallpaper, and Scandi-chic furniture decorate the clean and compact space. Although the apartment is advertised as a one-bedroom (a king), there is an additional small space with two twin beds, perfect for little ones. If you like to be in the thick of it, the central location makes it the perfect jumping-off point to explore nearby night markets and the various neighborhoods along the Chao Phraya River, visible from your condo.

Neighborhood: SilomThings to do nearby: Sky Bar, Bangkokian Museum, River City Bangkok culture and lifestyle center

Number of guests: 3Bed and bath: 1 bedroom, 1 bathWhy we love it: Fantastic lighting, standout bathroom, great location

Channeling the love den of Don Draper, this super-sexy, dimly lit studio is the perfect honeymoon rental. Inside an old shophouse, it’s a fourth-floor walk-up with midcentury-modern furniture, antique framed posters, a queen bed, and a small private balcony overlooking the buzzy Ratchathewi neighborhood. Dark wood and recessed lighting outfit the entire space, except for the striking bathroom, which is finished with olive green tiles and a large soaking tub (of note, there's no separate shower), perfect for bubble baths.

Neighborhood: RatchathewiThings to do nearby: Jim Thompson House Museum, Victory Monument

Number of guests: 6Bed and bath: 3 bedrooms, 3 bathsWhy we love it: Unique design, open-air living, stylish bathrooms

Neighborhood: RattanakosinThings to do nearby: Phra Sumen Fort, Khao San Road, The Marble Temple

What are the best neighborhoods to stay in Bangkok?

Chinatown and Talat Noi are always my go-to neighborhoods when I'm in Bangkok. They are full of fun, trendy bars, restaurants, and cafés worth spending some time wandering around. Sukhumvit is a great neighborhood for first-timers, with plenty of restaurant options, rooftop bars, and access to the MRT.

When is the best season to visit Bangkok?

Many people suggest that the best time to visit Bangkok is at the end of the rainy season—October through December—before the smog gets bad in January. March to May is the hottest time to visit, so it may be best to avoid if you don't do well in the heat, but I highly recommend planning a trip around Songkran (April 13–15), a.k.a. Thai New Year. It's known for hosting the world's largest water fight, and in my opinion, is one of Asia's best festivals.

#6229. Delta SkyMiles Gold Card Review: Solid Perks For Occasional Delta Flyers

The Delta SkyMiles® Gold American Express Card is the mid-range personal credit card in the American Express and Delta co-brand card portfolio, which includes seven cards, covering a variety of annual fee levels, across both personal and business products.

This post is my in-depth review of the Delta SkyMiles Gold Amex Card. The card has a reasonable annual fee and is ideal for someone looking for basic benefits that come in handy when flying Delta. However, if you’re a Medallion elite flyer on Delta, another card might be a better option (more on that below).

Link: Learn more about the Delta SkyMiles® Gold American Express Card

Before I get into my Delta Gold SkyMiles American Express Card review, here’s a quick look at the card’s main selling points and fees:

Here are my thoughts on the pros and cons of the Delta Gold SkyMiles Credit Card:

To start, let’s take a look at the Delta Gold Amex welcome bonus and ongoing fees, since these are some of the most important features to consider when opening a new card.

The Delta Gold SkyMiles Amex is currently offering new cardholders the following bonus: You may be eligible for as high as 80,000 Bonus Miles after you spend $2,000 in eligible purchases on your new Card in your first 6 months of Card Membership. Welcome offers vary and you may not be eligible for an offer.

Based on my latest miles & points valuations, SkyMiles are worth 1.1 cents each. That means to me, the welcome bonus is worth up to $880.

This is a solid welcome bonus, though the card recently offered a higher one that included a statement credit along with bonus miles. Everyone has to decide for themselves whether they’d rather wait for a better offer, or apply with this offer so they can take advantage of the perks ASAP.

The welcome offer on the Delta Gold Amex card is “once in a lifetime,” so it’s not available to you if you currently have the card, or if you’ve had the card in the past.

You’re also not eligible for the welcome offer on this card if you have or have had the personal versions of the Delta SkyMiles® Platinum American Express Card (learn more) or the Delta SkyMiles® Reserve American Express Card (learn more). However, you are eligible for this card if you’ve had any version of the business Delta Amex cards before.

One thing worth emphasizing is that if you’re going to apply for multiple personal Delta Amex cards, you’ll want to pick up the Delta Gold Amex first. That’s because if you do, you’d potentially still be eligible for the Delta Platinum Amex and Delta Reserve Amex. Meanwhile if you apply for one of those cards first, you’d no longer be eligible for the “lesser” card.

When it comes to credit scores, there’s not a consistent score you need to get approved for the Delta Gold Amex. I’d hope to have a score in the “good” to “excellent” range, ideally 700+ points. However, people with lower scores have been approved, and people with higher scores have been denied, as it’s only one of many factors that determines card eligibility.

You can read more about Amex’s general application restrictions here.

The Delta Gold SkyMiles American Express Card has a $0 introductory annual fee for the first year, then $150. (Rates & Fees). This is a great opportunity to try the card before you have to “buy” it. The card also has a reasonable annual fee on an ongoing basis, so it’s easy to recoup that fee by taking advantage of the card perks.

You can also add authorized users to the Delta Gold Amex at no extra cost.

If you are going to put spending on the card, the good news is that there are no foreign transaction fees (Rates & Fees) with the Delta Gold Amex, so you can use the card abroad without paying those high fees.

When applying for a credit card, the rewards structure is obviously a major consideration for people. With airline credit cards, the question typically comes down to both the miles offered on spending, as well as the ability to qualify for elite status with spending. Unfortunately the Delta Gold Amex isn’t much to get excited about on that front, but let’s still go over the details.

When it comes to the return on spending, the Delta Gold Card offers:

While it’s nice that the card has some bonus categories, I don’t find the bonuses to be particularly compelling. There are still better cards out there for airfare purchases, restaurant purchases, and grocery store purchases.

Nowadays it’s common to see airlines offer elite status qualification through credit card spending. Delta SkyMiles elite status is based on the concept of Medallion Qualifying Dollars (MQDs), and it’s possible to earn elite status with credit card spending.

The catch is that the Delta Gold Card doesn’t earn any MQDs, so if you want to qualify for status, you’ll have to pick up the Delta Platinum Card or Delta Reserve Card. More on that later.

While Delta SkyMiles is far from my favorite mileage currency, it does have a high floor value, so there are good ways to redeem Delta SkyMiles. You can redeem SkyMiles for flights on Delta or on Delta’s SkyTeam partners, like Air France, China Airlines, and Korean Air.

Partner award flights can be an especially good option if you focus on flights that don’t touch the United States, since flights that do are more expensive and get you less value for your miles. I’ve also seen some good award prices for Delta One (business class) awards, specifically for booking roundtrip rather than one way.

As I’ll cover below, having the Delta Gold Amex also gives you access to the TakeOff 15 discount on award tickets, and that can also help you stretch your SkyMiles for travel on Delta.

The real reason you’ll want to keep the Delta Gold Card long term is because of the perks and benefits that it offers, which are great for the casual Delta flyer. Truthfully, this is the value proposition of many airline credit cards — it’s largely about the welcome bonus and the perks, so let’s take a closer look at those details for the Delta Gold Amex.

Perhaps one of the biggest incentives to actually spend money on the Delta Gold SkyMiles Credit Card is the ability to earn a flight credit. Specifically, if you spend $10,000 on the card in a calendar year, you can receive a $200 Delta eCredit to use toward future travel, which will be deposited right in your SkyMiles account. The credit expires one year after it’s issued.

Getting a $200 Delta eCredit in addition to any miles could be a good incentive to spend $10,000 on the card per year. The credit alone is the equivalent of a 2% return on spending, assuming you consider it to be worth face value.

Just for having the Delta Gold Card you receive up to $100 in Delta Stays credit annually. The way this works, you receive up to $100 in statement credits per calendar year when you use your card to pay for a new Delta Stays prepaid hotel or vacation rental booking on the Delta Stays platform.

While I’m not usually a fan of using airline portals to book hotel stays and vacation rentals, this could prove worthwhile, as you can use it for a hotel stay costing right around $100, if you wanted to. If used right, the value here is considerable.

Just for having the Delta Gold SkyMiles Amex, you get a first checked bag free. You can also receive a second checked bag free on eligible domestic Delta flights.

This benefit is limited to the primary card member and up to eight companions traveling on the same reservation. You don’t have to pay for your flight with your Delta Amex, though you do need to have your SkyMiles number in the reservation.

With the ever-increasing cost of a checked bag with Delta, this can really add up. A first checked bag on domestic flights costs $45, and a second costs $55, so even just checking one bag on two roundtrip flights could effectively cancel out the card’s annual fee.

You receive priority boarding just for having the Delta Gold Amex. This helps maximize your odds of finding space for your carry-on and getting to your seat sooner. To receive this benefit, you must ensure the primary card member’s SkyMiles number is linked to the reservation. This benefit is valid for the primary card member and up to eight companions traveling on the same reservation.

If you have the Delta Gold Amex then you can save 20% in the form of a statement credit for eligible inflight purchases of food and beverages. The statement credit will post within 8-12 weeks of an eligible purchase.

Delta has a Pay With Miles feature, where if you have a Delta co-branded credit card, you can redeem miles for 1.0 cent each toward a Delta flight purchase (in increments of 5,000 miles per $50). That’s not the best deal in the world, though this is a feature that’s exclusively available to those with an eligible card.

Some people find this to be useful since they can redeem their miles toward flights, and then they still earn miles and MQDs on the portion of the fare they pay in cash.

With the Delta TakeOff 15 perk (exclusively for those with select Delta Amex cards), you can save 15% on the cost of a SkyMiles award ticket when traveling exclusively on Delta flights booked through delta.com or the Fly Delta app. Delta SkyMiles award pricing is dynamic, and generally you’ll find that each mile gets you a bit over a cent toward the cost of a ticket.

Saving 15% on these awards is valuable, and means that you’ll generally get somewhere around 1.2-1.3 cents of value per mile (or sometimes even more). In many cases this will end up being a better value than using the Pay With Miles option, so it’s a real perk of the card.

The Delta Gold SkyMiles Credit Card also comes with a rideshare credit. The way it works is that you get up to $10 back as a statement credits each month when you use the card on U.S. rideshare purchases with select providers, including Uber and Lyft.

You need to enroll in this benefit in order to get the money back, and it doesn’t kick in until after your first card renewal. So while it’s a useful perk if you already pay for rideshares at least once a month, it doesn’t really make or break the card.

One of the great features of Amex cards is access to Amex Offers, which offers savings or bonus points on purchases with all kinds of retailers. There’s huge value to be had in having as many Amex cards as possible, so that you can get these offers on multiple cards.

Amex Offers could save you hundreds of dollars per year. You can access these offers by logging into your account and scrolling down to the bottom of your account summary page. Note that enrollment is required to take advantage of individual offers.

The Delta Gold SkyMiles Credit Card comes with a handful of coverage benefits that can protect you and your belongings both at home and on the road, including:

There are some coverage limits and exclusions to be aware of, so you’ll want to review the full details in the card’s benefits guide before assuming you’re insured.

Baggage insurance plan: Eligibility and Benefit level varies by Card. Terms, Conditions, and Limitations Apply. Please visit americanexpress.com/benefitsguide for more details. Underwritten by AMEX Assurance Company. Car rental loss and damage insurance: Eligibility and Benefit level varies by Card. Terms, Conditions, and Limitations Apply. Please visit americanexpress.com/benefitsguide for more details. Underwritten by AMEX Assurance Company. Car Rental Loss or Damage Coverage is offered through American Express Travel Related Services Company, Inc. Extended warranty and purchase protection: Eligibility and Benefit level varies by Card. The Delta Gold SkyMiles Credit Card isn’t a card I’d be using for my everyday spending, since there are many more rewarding cards for that. However:

In other words, for someone who flies Delta occasionally, I think this card could make sense, and the benefits can more than offset the annual fee.

Meanwhile if you’re a more frequent Delta flyer, there could be value to having one of the more premium credit cards, which allow you to spend your way to elite status, and earn Medallion Qualification Dollars (MQDs).

If the Delta Gold Card sounds interesting to you, but you want a business card instead, consider the Delta SkyMiles® Gold Business American Express Card. Learn more about applying for Amex business cards.

The Delta SkyMiles® Blue American Express Card (learn more) has a $0 annual fee (Rates & Fees), and offers the following benefits:

Beyond that, though, there are limited perks. If you’d get value out of a first checked bag free or priority boarding, then you’re much better off getting one of Delta’s cards with an annual fee. I can’t really see much upside to getting the Delta Blue Card, over the other options in the market.

The Delta Platinum Amex (learn more) has a higher annual fee of $350 (Rates & Fees) and offers more perks than the Delta Gold:

If you want to earn MQDs toward elite status and enjoy more Delta benefits, like an annual companion certificate, the Delta Platinum Amex is the better option between these two cards.

The Delta Reserve Card (learn more) is the most premium option among personal Delta Amex cards, with the highest annual fee: $650 (Rates & Fees)

It also has the most benefits, so it could be worth it if you frequently fly Delta and want the best perks like lounge access:

Those aren’t even all the Delta Reserve card benefits. It also lets you earn MQDs on spending and gets you upgrade priority over other Delta SkyMiles members with your same Medallion tier, product, and fare experience purchased. The annual fee is high, but it’s absolutely worth a look if you want as many Delta perks as possible.

If you are looking to earn Delta SkyMiles through credit card spending then consider using a card earning Amex Membership Rewards points. That’s because these points can be transferred to Delta SkyMiles at a 1:1 ratio, and you can in many cases earn points at a much faster rate.

For example, the American Express® Gold Card (learn more) offers:

Furthermore, earning Amex points gives you more flexibility to redeem in other ways, given all the great uses of Membership Rewards points.

The Delta Gold SkyMiles Credit Card is a card that can be worth holding onto for the benefits that it offers, like up to $100 in Delta Stays credit, free checked bags, priority boarding, inflight savings, and more.

For the more frequent Delta flyer, consider the Delta Platinum Card, which can offer a larger bonus and additional perks, but also has a higher annual fee. Meanwhile if you’re a true Delta frequent flyer, consider the Delta Reserve Card, which offers some lounge access perks, helps you qualify for status fastest, etc.

As soon as you apply for a credit card, your application is processed by a computer. You’ll typically receive one of three responses: immediate approval, some form of “pending” status or denial.

Receiving instant approval doesn’t guarantee that you can begin using your card immediately. If you receive instant approval, you may be able to view your card number right away; otherwise, you’ll usually need to wait until your physical card arrives in the mail before you can begin using it.

It can take five to 10 business days to get a new credit card after approval. However, that timeframe varies by card and issuer. For instance, American Express offers overnight shipping for its top-tier cards. Some issuers offer expedited shipping on request, but there’s no guarantee. You may need to pay when requesting expedited shipping from some banks (including Barclays).

The Points Guy believes that credit cards can transform lives, helping you leverage everyday spending for cash back or travel experiences that might otherwise be out of reach. We publish editorial content and card reviews to help you find a great card to turn your goals into reality.

Getting approved for a new credit card is exciting, but waiting a week or more for it to arrive in the mail isn't. Fortunately, some issuers let you start using your new card immediately after approval, either by providing an instant card number or by allowing you to add your card to a digital wallet.

That instant access can give you a head start on meeting the welcome bonus spending requirement, since the clock starts ticking as soon as your account is approved — not when your physical card arrives. It can also come in handy if you need to make a purchase right away, whether you're booking travel or taking advantage of a 0% introductory APR offer. For cobranded store credit cards, you may also receive a discount on your purchases, starting as soon as you use the card.

Here's a look at which major credit card issuers offer instant card numbers, digital wallet access or both.

Some issuers provide an instant card number, while others, like Chase, instead let eligible cardholders add their new card to a digital wallet immediately after approval. Both options let you start using your card before the physical version arrives.

While there are too many cards to list that offer instant card numbers or access, here are six of our top picks.

American Express provides your new account number immediately after your online application is approved, provided your identity can be verified.

The instant card number will be the same as the physical card you’ll get in the mail, but the four-digit card identification number on the front of the card will be different. Because of that, you may want to wait to set up recurring payments.

Note that instant card numbers for some cobranded cards may only be used with the cobranded company (like Delta, Hilton or Marriott).

In addition to instant numbers for new cardmembers, Amex gives existing cardmembers access to their card information when ordering replacement cards.

Most Amex personal and business cards offer instant card numbers; notable exclusions include the Amazon Business Card and the Amazon Business Prime Card.

The information for the Amazon Business and Amazon Business Prime cards have been collected independently by The Points Guy. The card details on this page have not been reviewed or provided by the card issuer.

Occasionally, those with Bank of America checking accounts may receive a targeted promotion offering an instant card number for cards like the ; however, this is not standard practice.

You may be able to receive an instant card number by applying through the Bank of America app, but data points on this vary. Unless you already have an established relationship with Bank of America, you should plan on waiting for a physical card to arrive before use.

Related: The best Bank of America credit cards

With Barclays, you may be eligible to receive a virtual card number upon approval. When added to a digital wallet, this number can be used to make purchases until your physical card arrives.

You should be able to retrieve your virtual card number on the same page where you check your application status, provided you're approved for the card.

Capital One Mobile app users may be able to use instant card numbers immediately after they’re approved, before their physical card arrives in the mail.

This differs from Capital One's virtual card numbers, which are designed to help protect your purchases rather than provide immediate access to a newly approved account.

Cardless focuses on cobranded credit cards you can use without a physical card. These are available instantly upon approval and can be used throughout the life of the card.

Through the Cardless app, you can access these cobranded cards and even get a new card number immediately if your card is ever compromised.

Cardless provides cobranded credit cards for brands like Avianca, Bilt and LATAM Airlines.

It is possible to use popular Chase cards instantly upon account approval by adding them to a digital wallet via Spend Instantly. These include the , (see rates and fees) and (see rates and fees).

It's important to note that this does not include a way to access an instant card number, but a way to instantly add your card to a digital wallet.

Here are the steps to set up Spend Instantly.

However, the issuer notes that several cards cannot be used immediately, including Mastercards, Amazon cards and business cards.

Citi offers instant card numbers for select cards if your application is approved instantly and your identity is verified. If eligible, you'll see a "Get Card Number Today" option after approval, followed by "See Card Summary" to view your temporary card number and security code. You’ll have just one opportunity to view this number, so be sure to write it down.

The (see rates and fees) works differently: Eligible applicants may receive a temporary barcode that can be used only for Costco purchases.

Availability varies by card and instant credit card numbers are not available on small-business or American Airlines credit cards, according to a Citi spokesperson. Some readers have also reported not having the option to get an instant card number with cards like the (see rates and fees).

Discover often gives you an instant decision on whether you’ve been approved for a credit card. After this decision, if eligible, you can receive a virtual card number to use online or add to a digital wallet.

The Discover it® Cash Back is our top pick. It is a good card for beginners and has rotating 5% quarterly cash-back categories.

SoFi's credit cards offer instant digital access, with physical cards arriving in the mail within 10 business days. These cards include:

The first two options offer great cash back. The SoFi Unlimited offers unlimited 2% cash back on all purchases. Meanwhile, the SoFi Everyday offers up to 3% bonus cash back in a variety of categories, including dining and groceries.

There are two Synchrony cards you can use immediately upon approval. However, you’ll only be able to use them instantly within digital wallets or within their respective apps: PayPal (for the PayPal Cashback Mastercard®) and Venmo (for the Venmo Credit Card).

You’ll need to wait for your card to arrive by mail before you can make purchases through other methods.

Wells Fargo generally does not offer instant card numbers, but you may be able to add your card to a digital wallet. Where you can use this virtual card may be restricted until your physical card arrives.

Some issuers offer expedited shipping for your new card. In most cases, though, you’ll have to wait roughly a week for your new card to arrive in the mail. Having instant access to your new card details can make a meaningful difference when you're working toward a valuable welcome bonus or need to make a purchase right away.

#6227. ATMA: Aman’s New Brand, Debuting With A 1,049-Foot Miami Tower

Aman is known for being one of the world’s top luxury hotel groups. Currently Aman Group consists of Aman (the original hotel group) and Janu (intended to be more of a “lifestyle” version of Aman). Aman is now launching a third brand, and it’s yet another departure from the origins of Aman.

Aman Group has announced the launch of ATMA, described as a “new ultra-luxury brand pioneering performance living.” ATMA means “the spirit” or “the true self” in Sanskrit, and the intent is for the brand to combine wellness, sport, nutrition-led dining, design, and experiential entertainment.

ATMA will “focus on advanced wellness programming and world-class sport facilities, which have been developed exclusively by ATMA Global Partner Novak Djokovic.”

The first location will be ATMA Miami, and it will include a hotel, branded residence, and a private members club. Specifically, the property will be in the Brickell neighborhood and will have a private marina, with an anticipated opening in 2031.

ATMA Miami is expected to be a standalone 1,049-foot tower, which is as tall as buildings can get in Miami. In terms of height, it’ll be match the new 100-story Waldorf Astoria Miami that’s currently under construction, which will be the tallest building in Florida, once complete.

Details about ATMA Miami are still fairly limited, but we know there will be 480 residential units, in addition to the hotel. Residential units will be between one and six bedrooms, and will be “supported by Aman Group’s service standards.”

There will also be a 120,000 square foot spa and wellness area, set to be the largest of its kind in Miami. Developed in partnership with Djokovic, it will offer performance and recovery experiences alongside indoor padel, tennis and squash courts, a fitness center, group and private training studios, mobility and conditioning labs, a medical wellness center, and dedicated recovery spaces.

So far we’ve only learned about the Miami location, but the claim is that the brand will span urban and remote destinations.

Look, I’ve made my opinions about the Aman brand pretty clear, so I don’t want to sound like some old dude just ranting about the “good old days.” When Aman was founded by hospitality legend Adrian Zecha, it was truly among the most innovative and passion driven hospitality projects we’ve ever seen.

In 2014, Zecha sold the brand to Vladislav Doronin, and since then, the entire philosophy has changed. It’s hard to fault someone for purchasing a brand and trying to cash in and maximize profitability — I mean, that’s kind of how the business world is supposed to work, right?

But of course that doesn’t mean we have to be happy about the evolution. It started with Aman ditching its approach of largely opening hotels in the middle of nowhere, where that was part of the charm. Instead, we saw Aman focus on city hotels. Then Aman became all about opening members clubs. Then we saw the launch of the Janu brand, essentially a higher room count version of Aman, with a more lively spirit.

And now we’re seeing Aman getting into building full-on skyscrapers. Well, or at least partnering on them in terms of branding. Of course some Aman properties already have a residences component, so that’s nothing new, as such. However, the scale of this project couldn’t be more opposite of what Aman initially was. We’re talking about a 100-story building that will have nearly 500 residences, and who knows how many hotel rooms (it hasn’t yet been announced).

Of course in Miami, one of the biggest trends is branded residences, with brands just selling out their name. But if Aman were to just slap its name on a residential project, you’d think it would be something smaller scale than this. This is among the highest unit count developments we’ve ever seen in Miami, at least for a project spanning just one building.

Aman Group has just announced its third brand, and it will be named ATMA. It’s described as a “new ultra-luxury brand pioneering performance living.” The first location will open in Miami in 2031, and it’ll be a roughly 100-story building with 480 residences, a hotel, and a members club.

Aman as a brand has become unrecognizable compared to what it was 15 years ago. But that’s fair enough, and it’s also what happens when you sell a company to someone looking to maximize their ROI. You can hardly fault someone for that, as much as I don’t personally like it.

#6226. Will Credit Card Interest Rates Be Capped At 10%? Democrats Want To Work With Trump

With the recent midterm elections, the balance of power in Washington is very quickly changing. Given the extent to which things shifted left, Democrats certainly want to be able to show that they can accomplish something in the next two years, to make life better for average Americans.

Along those lines, we’re once again seeing a proposal floated regarding capping credit card interest rates. There’s a lot more support for this than in the past, given the majority that Democrats have, plus the fact that President Trump has also been in support of this concept (or at least claimed to be). Will it actually pass, though?

Senate Democrats are renewing a proposal to cap credit card interest rates at 10%, with Elizabeth Warren of Massachusetts specifically bringing this up in a “Face The Nation” interview. Warren is likely to chair the Senate Banking Committee, and could use her position to help advance the proposal.

Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-MA) says she wants to work with President Trump to cap credit card interest rates at 10% and Democrats “have the bills ready to go” to work with the president. “We got a whole bunch more that the American people have told us that they want on price… pic.twitter.com/0r17PwXPQT

Now, before anyone gets political, keep in mind that this is a concept that Trump actually proposed earlier this year. He claimed that Americans were being ripped off by credit card companies, and that as of January 20, 2026, credit card interest rates should be capped at 10%. However, this just came in the form of a social media post, rather than any actual legislation:

Please be informed that we will no longer let the American Public be “ripped off” by Credit Card Companies that are charging Interest Rates of 20 to 30%, and even more, which festered unimpeded during the Sleepy Joe Biden Administration. AFFORDABILITY! Effective January 20, 2026, I, as President of the United States, am calling for a one year cap on Credit Card Interest Rates of 10%. Coincidentally, the January 20th date will coincide with the one year anniversary of the historic and very successful Trump Administration. Thank you for your attention to this matter. MAKE AMERICA GREAT AGAIN! PRESIDENT DONALD J. TRUMP

Donald J. Trump Truth Social Post 08:10 PM EST 01.09.26 pic.twitter.com/47SQ03yMeo

Unsurprisingly, there was no enforcement mechanism, and this never happened, especially since he got pushback from other Republicans. If he really believed in that proposal, then it sounds like this will be his chance to actually turn it into some sort of a law, with support from Democrats. We’ll have to mark this as “developing” for now.

Just for some context, credit card issuers make money in three primary ways — through interchange fees, through interest charges, and through annual fees. When it comes to interest rates, credit card companies are known for having very high rates, an average of over 20%. These are the charges that apply if you don’t pay your full balance before the payment due date. You don’t pay interest charges if you simply charge your purchase to a credit card, and then pay your balance in full.

On the surface, capping credit card interest rates of course sounds great — some of the rates are really high, and many people view banks as greedy, and think they can afford to give up some of their margins. Obviously for those who are currently financing charges, a cap on interest rates would be positive.

The thing is, a policy change like this wouldn’t come without some other changes. There’s no denying that if interest rates were capped at 10%, lots of consumers with not-great credit would be locked out of getting credit cards, and might even have their accounts closed, because card issuers would find it too risky to loan them money at that rate.

After all, there’s a huge risk to people not making payments, and the economics of that work differently with 10% interest rates rather than 25% interest rates. I would imagine that tens of millions of Americans would have their accounts closed, that we’d see fewer no annual fee cards, etc.

Beyond that, if we did see a long term cap on credit card interest rates, it would likely change the credit card landscape in terms of how rewarding cards are, with everything ranging from welcome bonuses, to rewards on spending, to perks.

Right or wrong, credit card economics are heavily reliant on a cross-subsidized system. That’s the whole reason some of us are able to get such outsized value. Credit card rewards structures nowadays largely more or less rebate back interchange fees to consumers, as it’s easy to earn 2% cash back with cards, or even to earn huge multipliers on spending.

The reality is that the revenue that subsidizes a lot of rewards is the interest charges, since that’s the highest margin revenue stream from many card issuers. So we’re partly earning huge welcome bonuses and 5x points on some transactions because someone else is paying close to 30% interest.

I’m not saying that’s a good system, but I’m just being realistic about how it works. If interest rates are forced to be slashed by more than half in the long run, it will have major implications for rewards. Maybe that’s objectively not a bad thing, but it will happen.

For that matter, it would even have a major impact on airlines — they’re so reliant on credit card revenue nowadays to turn profits, and this would greatly hurt their margins in that area as well.

With Democrats soon controlling both the House and Senate, there’s a renewed push to cap credit card interest rates at 10%. This is a proposal that Trump made earlier this year, but it didn’t get support from Republicans.

While I totally appreciate that credit card interest rates are often incredibly high, it’s not without reason, given the rate of default on some cards. Approval standards for cards would change, many consumers would have their cards shut down, etc. It would also likely change the economics of the credit card industry, which could even impact airlines.

However, I’m not some lobbyist or apologist for the credit card industry. If the change happens, many people will benefit, and I’m sure the industry will adapt. However, unarguably many people will go from paying 25% interest on their credit card, to potentially paying even higher rates for payday loans, doing business with loan sharks, etc.

What do you make of this proposal to cap credit card interest rates?

#6225. Report: Google Accepts Privacy Safeguards for Spirit Data

The Wall Street Journal reported Monday that the proposed sale will exclude personnel records, including medical files, results of drug and alcohol tests, performance reviews, payroll information, and grievance and arbitration filings.

Unions representing former Spirit pilots and flight attendants had objected to the inclusion of that data, noting Google’s plans to use the information to train its artificial intelligence models. The agreement reached this week resolves the unions’ concerns, the Journal said.

Google and Spirit initially planned to have an outside company “deidentify” the airline’s records. That process will still take place, though at a higher standard than Spirit intended to use, and Google will be prohibited from attempting to “reidentify” the data.

Spirit went out of business in May following a dramatic rise in jet fuel prices. The decision to auction off its internal records for use by AI was a first for the airline industry and opened up a new realm of contestation for workers and employers.

#6224. 5 Busy Airports Where Intersecting Runways Complicate Takeoffs & Landings

Perhaps the most ideal layout for an airport is the 'pinwheel' arrangement at Denver International Airport (DEN). This allows multiple sets of parallel runways in different directions to operate largely independently. This increases capacity, reduces taxi times, and there are no intersections. However, the problem is that the pinwheel arrangement takes up a significant amount of space, and many airfields simply lack the land to design such a layout. Still, adding runways is primarily how airfields boost capacity.

Many older airports operate with intersecting runways, which represent a compromise for airports that need to add capacity but are limited on space. These arrangements can have lower capacity because intersections require more spacing to accommodate arrivals and departures in certain cases. Using intersecting runways simultaneously also requires added coordination to ensure safety. Still, several major hubs use intersecting runways, including some of the busiest airports in the United States.

LaGuardia Airport (LGA) is the smallest of the three primary airports serving the New York metropolitan region, alongside JFK and Newark. However, it is also the one located closest to Manhattan, making it the most desirable airport for business travelers, as it takes less time to travel from LGA to the city. As such, there's heavy demand for flights to destinations within the 1,500-mile (2,414 km) perimeter limit. Demand to LGA is high, but the airport lacks the capacity to truly accommodate the demand.

LaGuardia originally opened with four runways, two of which have since closed. The remaining runways, which have been extended since the airport's opening, are numbered 4/22 and 13/31, and each is 7,002 feet (2,134 meters). They intersect at the northwestern part of the airfield, which can complicate daily operations. Controllers typically use one runway for departures and one for arrivals, so planes must be sequenced carefully to prevent conflicts.

John F. Kennedy International Airport (JFK)

Newark Liberty International Airport (EWR)

Demand for LaGuardia far outstrips the airport's flight capacity, making it one of only three slot-restricted airports in the US (alongside JFK and Washington National). The intersecting runways mean its practical flight capacity is lower than if the airport had two parallel runways. However, LaGuardia has been around for nearly 90 years, and it's severely restricted on space as it's surrounded by either residential neighborhoods or water. As such, it will remain a constrained airfield.

Chicago Midway International Airport (MDW) served as the primary airport for Chicago until O'Hare Airport opened in the 1950s. Since then, airlines have generally preferred O'Hare, although Midway remains active. Today, over 90% of the airport's commercial operations come from Southwest Airlines, which has established MDW as a major operating base. In addition, Midway also receives regular flights from Allegiant Air, Delta Air Lines, Frontier, and Volaris, although these operations are comparatively tiny.

The airport has four runways, numbered 4L/22R, 4R/22L, 13L/31R, and 13R/31L. The last one, 13R/31L, is significantly shorter than the rest and is primarily used for light aircraft, while the airliners use the other three runways. Runways 13R and 31L intersect both 4L/22R and 4R/22L, while the parallel 13L/31R also intersects both runways. This creates four runway intersections, requiring careful coordination by air traffic control and vigilance from pilots on the ground to maintain safety.

MDW is landlocked on all sides, which means that it has practically no room to expand or revise the runway layout. The airport is not at capacity, so the runway layout is not a major commercial issue. However, it does require extra caution due to the added risk of having four runways that intersect at four different points. In addition, there are difficulties with the airport's general layout, including the much shorter and narrower Runway 13R/31L, which can be confused for a taxiway.

How Gatwick handles over 43 million passengers annually with one runway through world-class scheduling, rapid turnarounds, and operational efficiency.

Detroit Metropolitan Wayne County Airport (DTW) is a major hub for Delta Air Lines, which operates it as a midcontinent connecting hub with significant service to Europe and Asia. It is a fortress hub for Delta, which holds over 70% market share at the airport and connects Detroit to over 100 destinations around the US and the world. It's a busy hub with well over 300,000 aircraft movements annually, 147 gates, two main terminals, as well as six runways in total. Two of them run east-west, while the remaining four run north-south.

The two east-west runways are numbered 9L/27R and 9R/27L, while the four parallel north-south runways are numbered 3L/21R, 3R/21L, 4L/22R, and 4R/22L. Runway 9R/27L crosses Runway 3R/21L, while Runway 9L/27R crosses Runway 3R/21L, 3L/21R, and 4R/22L. The only runway at DTW that does not intersect with another is Runway 4L/22R, located at the westernmost part of the airfield and running parallel to the other north-south runways.

Although there are four intersection points, DTW rarely actually uses Runways 9L/27R and 9R/27L. Instead, it mainly operates using the four north-south parallel runways, which intersect the east-west runways but not each other. As such, the intersection points rarely play a significant role in everyday operations. Instead, Runways 9L/27R and 9R/27L are used when winds would produce an unusually strong crosswind on the north-south parallel runways.

San Francisco International Airport (SFO) is one of the most unique airports in the US. Bounded on three sides by water and on the fourth by residential developments, the airport is quite space-constrained. It operates four runways, with two sets of parallel runways set perpendicular to one another. The two pairs of runways intersect each other, creating four intersection points. The airport is famous for its simultaneous approaches, but it also often runs simultaneous departures, particularly with narrowbody aircraft.

The operations of SFO require intense coordination, with departures and arrivals having to be staggered to prevent conflicts as SFO often uses both runway pairs. Recently, however, the FAA prohibited SFO from continuing its longstanding practice of operating side-by-side landings, instead requiring planes to be offset from one another. This significantly reduced the airport's arrival capacity, leading to additional delays due to weather or congestion as the airport becomes increasingly constrained.

SFO serves as the primary hub for United Airlines, which uses it as its primary gateway to Asia and Oceania. The airline has over 50% market share, and United connects San Francisco to over 120 destinations worldwide. The airport serves one of the biggest business markets in the country, and international traffic is surging. However, it's also becoming increasingly constrained by its runway layout, while frequent fog results in weather delays far more often than airlines, passengers, and the airport would like.

The world's largest airports will soon offer much more capacity.

Boston Logan International Airport (BOS) has one of the most unusual runway layouts of any airport in the US. It has six runways, including what are technically two sets of parallel runways. The runways are numbered 4L/22R, 4R/22L, 9/27, 14/32, 15L/33R, and 15R/33L. There are six intersections in total, although the runways are not used equally. Runway 15L/33R, at only 2,557 feet (779 meters) long, is used solely by light aircraft, while the runways that are used by airliners are assigned depending on the winds.

BOS is locked on all sides, with limited land available and no room for expansion. The arrangement of the different runways allows the airport to more easily accommodate flights during shifting winds, which can change very often in a given day, without compromising on arrival capacity. Runways 4L/22R and 4R/22L are often the runways most commonly used by air traffic controllers at BOS, but the airport can easily switch directions if weather conditions necessitate it, while the arrangement provides more flexibility.

Boston Logan International Airport Runways

Although there are several intersection points at BOS, this doesn't complicate operations significantly. Unlike an airport such as LaGuardia or San Francisco, only a few runways are used at a time at BOS, and they usually follow the same direction. At LGA or SFO, controllers have to manage aircraft operating in multiple directions routinely, but this isn't the case at BOS or DTW. While the intersections reflect compromises due to a lack of space, they're not a major issue for BOS's operations specifically.

#6223. American First Class Will Get Mini-Meals On Shorter Flights (700-899 Miles)

American Airlines is making a very nice change to first class service on some short haul flights that didn’t previously qualify for a meal service, and it’s something I’m sure passengers will be happy to see.

As things currently stand, American serves meals in first class on flights of at least 900 miles during meal times (900 miles roughly correlates to a little over two hours of flying, on average). In the US, this is basically the industry standard, as Delta and United have the same cutoff of 900 miles for serving meals. On flights shorter than that, airlines only offer drinks and a snack basket in first class.

It looks like American will soon be leading the industry when it comes to service in first class on shorter flights, as it brings back a program it used to offer. JonNYC was first to report that American will be bringing back the “light bites” concept on flights of 700 to 899 miles (700 miles correlates to a little over 90 minutes of flying, on average).

AA:"Light bites”/mini-meals coming back to short haul domestic first class flights 700-899 milesStarting on NYC/ORD.

As now confirmed by American, this is launching this month on flights between Chicago (ORD) and New York, including Kennedy (JFK) and LaGuardia (LGA). It remains to be seen when it expands to other routes. It must be a decade at this point since American offered this concept.

The expectation is that there will be a rotating selection of options, with two available on each flight, and they won’t be available via pre-order.

Breakfast selections may include smoked salmon, tropical chia overnight oats, prosciutto and melon, fruit and cheese plates, prosciutto and brie, or apple cinnamon chia pudding. Lunch and dinner options may include curry chicken salads, Thai noodle salads, turkey and gouda sandwiches, whipped burrata, poached shrimp with noodle salads, mezze plates, blackened chicken, or grilled vegetable wraps.

It goes without saying that expectations of premium cabin travelers differ massively around the globe. In the Middle East, it’s common to have a 30-minute business class flight with a lie flat bed, cappuccinos, champagne, and a substantial, tasty snack.

In Europe, you’re typically stuck with a pretty underwhelming hard product on short haul flights (just economy with a blocked middle), but regardless of the length of the flight, you’re almost always served something fresh, even if the flight time is well under an hour.

In the United States, we have the benefit of actually having a dedicated first class cabin with larger seats, but the soft product just isn’t great. You can be on a flight of nearly two hours and just be served packaged snacks.

We do have to give credit to Alaska for this, as it’s the only US carrier to serve some sort of fresh food on flights of under 900 miles. On most Alaska flights you’ll get a snack on shorter services, so kudos to the airline for that.

American Airlines will once again serve fresh food in first class on flights of 700-899 miles. This concept will debut on flights between Chicago and New York, and passengers will have the choice of two rotating options. This is really a resumption of something that American offered many years back.

Among the “big three” US carriers, American will be the only one to serve fresh food in first class on flights of under 900 miles, so kudos to the airline for that.

What do you make of American serving mini-meals on shorter first class flights?

Call it the ultimate Nile River cruise experience.

River cruise giant Viking has unveiled an epic new itinerary that sails the entire 600-mile stretch of the waterway between Cairo in the north and Aswan in the south.

Dubbed the Grand Nile Journey, Viking's 19-day trip revives a longer Nile cruise route that dates back to the late 1800s, when paddle steamers carried travelers from Cairo on the 465-mile journey south to Luxor, home to some of ancient Egypt's most famous temples and burial grounds.

From there, the vessels would continue to Aswan, another 130 miles to the south, with stops at ancient temples along the way.

Nowadays, most Nile River sailings skip the first 465 miles of this historic route, with ships only traveling along the 130-mile stretch of the Nile between Luxor and Aswan. Passengers reach the ships by flying from Cairo to Luxor, typically after a few days exploring Cairo.

Related: The ultimate guide to Nile river cruises and cruisetours

Only a handful of vessels currently operate a longer itinerary of the sort that Viking has announced — and none at the luxury level for which Viking is known on the river.

Kicking off in 2028 but available to book now, Viking's new Grand Nile Journeys will begin with a three-night stay at a luxury hotel in Cairo (the line often puts guests in the elegant Fairmont Nile City, along the banks of the river). Then, passengers board the line's one-of-a-kind, all-suite vessel Viking Ra for the 14-night journey south to Aswan.

The voyages will include stops at ancient sites along the 450-mile stretch from Cairo to Luxor that most Nile River travelers never see, including the 4,600-year-old Meidum Pyramid near Beni Suef and the striking cliffside Noble Tombs of Beni Hasan.

Other rare stops will include a visit to Tell el-Amarna, the once-lost royal desert capital founded by the Pharaoh Akhenaten, and the Abydos Temple, famous for drawings of ancient pilgrims to the sacred Festival of Osiris.

After a week traveling south along this lesser-visited stretch of the Nile, the Viking Ra will arrive in Luxor for another week of travel southward along the more popular parts of the river.

An extended stop in Luxor will bring visits to the temples of Luxor and Karnak, the royal tombs of the Valley of the Kings and the Temple of Seti I at Abydos.

Additional stops include the Temple of Horus in Edfu and the Temple of Philae near Aswan, among other sites in this area.

Related: The 5 best destinations you can visit on a Viking ship

By following this long route from Cairo to Aswan, the new Grand Nile Journeys will echo the long Nile sailing that Agatha Christie made famous in her 1937 novel "Death on the Nile." She wrote the book after taking one of the long journeys in 1933 on the Thomas Cook & Son luxury paddle steamer S.S. Sudan.

The first few days of each of the new Grand Nile Journeys in Cairo will include visits to the Great Pyramids of Giza, the Great Sphinx and the Grand Egyptian Museum.

At the end of the trip, passengers will also spend a final night at a hotel in Cairo before departing.

Passengers can extend their trips with optional pre- and postcruise land tours that include an extra two-night stay in Cairo and a four-night, fully guided excursion to nearby Jordan for visits to the Dead Sea, Petra and Amman.

While dating back to the late 1800s, when Thomas Cook & Son introduced "rapid steamers" that sailed the Nile from Cairo to Aswan, such longer Nile itineraries continued to be common until 1994, when the Egyptian government officially closed the 465-mile stretch of the river between Cairo and Luxor to overnight passenger ships due to security worries. Low water levels and shifting sandbars in the river also played a role.

After nearly 20 years of closure, the Egyptian government reopened the Cairo-to-Luxor stretch of the river to cruise vessels in 2012, following extensive river dredging, irrigation upgrades and major security overhauls. But long sailings from Cairo to Aswan have been slow to rebound.

Among the handful of other companies offering such trips is Movenpick Hotels & Resorts, which markets 14-night sailings from Cairo to Aswan on the 52-cabin MS Darakum.

The American Express® Business Gold Card is one of the most rewarding business cards if you’re looking to earn Amex Membership Rewards points.

We’re currently seeing an excellent Amex Business Gold Card welcome offer, which is the biggest bonus we’ve ever seen on the card, making it the ideal time to apply. If you’re eligible for this card and the highest possible bonus, it’s absolutely worth taking advantage of, in my opinion.

Link: Learn more about the American Express® Business Gold Card

The Amex Business Gold Card currently has a massive welcome offer that’s as high as 200,000 Membership Rewards points after spending $15,000 on eligible purchases within the first three months. Welcome offers vary and you may not be eligible for an offer. Find out your offer.

Amex uses a variety of factors when it comes to deciding what offer people are eligible for, including history of opening and closing cards with Amex, spending history with Amex, how many welcome offers people have earned, etc. So, how does this Amex Business Gold Card bonus actually work?

You should find the highest possible offer through the above link. However, if you don’t, it can always be worth checking refer-a-friend links, opting in to targeted emails from Amex, or even using the CardMatch tool to see what you’re eligible for there. That being said, don’t expect to get a higher offer through any of those sources, since offers are typically targeted based on the person, rather than the application method.

It goes without saying that the Amex Business Gold bonus spending requirement is potentially significant, as it averages out to $5,000 per month. However, there are lots of ways to be creative with reaching minimum spending, and to make a plan. You could time your application around some large upcoming business expenses (whether that’s an ad campaign or buying inventory), prepay for some items, and maybe even put some expenses on credit cards that you might otherwise pay for with cash. Of course make sure you pay off everything in full by the payment due date, so that you don’t get stuck paying high interest charges.

Based on my latest miles & points valuations, I consider Membership Rewards points to be worth 1.7 cents each. That means to me, 200,000 points are worth $3,400, which is an incredible offer, assuming you’re eligible. This is the biggest publicly available bonus that we’ve seen on this card, and in the past, we’ve often only seen offers of 70,000 to 100,000 points, so this is much better. I’d consider the Amex Business Gold Card bonus to be among the best welcome offers out there.

There are lots of great uses for Amex points, as they can be transferred to all kinds of useful airline and hotel partners, ranging from Air France-KLM Flying Blue, to Emirates Skywards, to Singapore Airlines KrisFlyer, to Virgin Atlantic Flying Club. There are a few additional things to note when it comes to applying for Amex business cards:

Anecdotally, I find this to be a pretty easy card to get approved for, and you can read about my experience applying here.

#6220. Aer Lingus Pilots Threatened With Criminal Charges Over Bomb Threat Diversion

Last week, I covered how dozens of flights across Europe were faced with bomb threats. It was clearly a hoax, but these have to be taken seriously, and we saw all kinds of diversions, flight cancelations, and more.

Europe’s largest union representing pilots is now sharing the details of an incident that happened with one of these diversions, whereby an Aer Lingus flight was forced by fighter jets to divert to a French military base. When the pilots weren’t comfortable doing so, they were reportedly threatened with criminal charges.

This incident happened on Thursday, November 5, 2026, and involves Aer Lingus flight EI402, scheduled to operate from Dublin (DUB) to Rome (FCO). The Airbus A320 with the registration code EI-DEH took off at 6:40AM local time, and made its way southeast toward Rome.

The A320 flew for around an hour, and made it just past Paris, when the plane changed heading and prepared to divert. French fighter jets had been deployed to escort the aircraft, and demanded that it divert to a French military base. Specifically, the plane diverted to Évreux-Fauville Air Base (EVX), located in Normandy.

The plane touched down there at 10:05AM local time, 2hr25min after it first departed (there was a one hour time change). Coincidentally, that’s basically the same flight time as it would’ve been to Rome, as the aircraft had to hold for an extended period of time.

The plane ended up returning to Dublin later in the day, departing at 4:59PM local time, and landing in Dublin at 5:20PM local time, after a flight time of 1hr21min. So passengers spent nearly 12 hours on the plane, only to end up back where they started. Man, that’s rough, especially when you consider these A320s don’t have power ports, Wi-Fi, etc.

Here’s where the story gets really interesting, as explained by the European Cockpit Association (ECA), which represents over 44,000 pilots across Europe, including pilots at Aer Lingus. The union is expressing serious concerns about how this incident was handled.

What happened is that the Aer Lingus pilots didn’t want to divert to Évreux-Fauville Air Base, because they didn’t have the necessary operational information and aeronautical charts to land there. They requested a landing at another airport, but were rejected. According to the pilots, they were even threatened with criminal charges if they didn’t divert to the airport as requested.

That’s the point on which the union is sounding the alarm. Let me just quote the union on this:

As representatives of the pilot profession, ECA, IALPA and SNPL fully recognise and appreciate the assistance provided by authorities in responding to these threats and supporting flight crews in bringing their passengers and aircraft to safety.

However, reports indicate that, in certain circumstances, military aircraft have intercepted civilian airliners and directed aircraft commanders to land at specific airports without adequately considering aircrafts’ operational and safety requirements.

According to information received by IALPA, in one recent incident involving an Aer Lingus aircraft, military fighter aircraft directed the flight crew to divert to a military airfield for which they did not have the necessary aeronautical charts and operational information to safely conduct a landing. Despite the flight crew seeking an alternative and more suitable diversion airport, their request was refused.

ECA, IALPA and SNPL are also alarmed by subsequent reports that the pilots were apparently faced by the prospect of possible criminal prosecution for actions that were, at all times, aimed at protecting their passengers, crew and aircraft.

The union emphasizes that the captain of a flight should have the ultimate responsibility for the safety of passengers, crew, and the aircraft, and that the captain is uniquely positioned to assess the operational circumstances and determine the safest course of action, taking account of all relevant factors, including aircraft performance, available aeronautical information, airport suitability, operational limitations, and the availability of emergency assistance on the ground.

The union points out how the prospect of criminal prosecution against pilots exercising their professional judgment in such circumstances risks undermining aviation safety, and the effective cooperation between flight crews and authorities.

An Aer Lingus A320 was recently forced to divert to a military base in France, after the aircraft faced a bomb threat (which also impacted dozens of other flights). Fighter jets reportedly demanded the plane divert to this airport despite objections from the pilots, who felt they didn’t have sufficient operational information and aeronautical charts to land there.

The union representing pilots claims that the pilots were threatened with criminal charges if they didn’t divert there, which the union believes undermines the responsibility that pilots should have over the safety of their aircraft.

I fully side with the pilots and union here. It’s silly to me that a bomb threat that’s an obvious hoax puts pilots in a situation where they don’t feel comfortable landing at, with no alternatives offered.

What do you make of this Aer Lingus pilot situation?

#6219. Severe Hail Storm Forces Inspections Of Over 2 Dozen American Airlines Jets In Philadelphia

Journalist – Aaron is an aviation and travel journalist with 14 years of experience in the travel and tourism industry. His background spans airport operations, aviation infrastructure, and travel consulting, having worked with global organizations across New Zealand, Europe, and North America. Combining industry expertise with firsthand travel experience across more than 52 countries and five continents, Aaron covers airlines, airports, aviation policy, and the wider travel sector. He is based in Canterbury, New Zealand. His work has been published in Simple Flying and featured by MSN, SAM CHUI Aviation & Travel, EIN News, Pakistan Defence, and Climate Depot.

An adverse weather event struck parts of Delaware County and parts of Pennsylvania on Thursday, leading to dozens of American Airlines aircraft needing to be inspected at Philadelphia International Airport (PHL). A heavy hailstorm resulted in parts of the city and airport looking like they had been covered in snow.

In a report by aviation insider JonNYC on X, the unexpected weather front forced American to hold two dozen aircraft shortly after the hailstorm. This allowed engineers to inspect the aircraft before they were cleared to fly.

An American-only ground stop following the hail resulted in delays and disruptions for many flights at Philadelphia, while general poor weather conditions in the country's northeast resulted in a total of 820 flights nationwide being delayed and a total of 65 being canceled, as reported by Oregon Live.

This was caused by low clouds, persistent rain, and wind that hampered services at the airports detailed above. These flight delays and cancelations saw thousands of travelers on late-arriving flights and further disruption to onward travel plans.

To ensure the safety of both the aircraft and those who were set to travel onboard, an American Airlines-only ground stop was implemented at Philadelphia to allow the assessment of the aircraft. This is due to the planes being exposed to the conditions while they were parked at the gate.

A number of inbound flights were also affected, with some passengers reporting long waits on aircraft parked at other US airports. These included AA2412 from Tampa (TPA), where a passenger posted on Reddit that they were stranded for up to three hours until weather conditions at their destination had improved.

Simple Flying reached out to American Airlines for comment on Thursday. However, an airline spokesperson could not immediately be reached.

Pilots consult dispatch and push for an alternate path as ATC initially points the flight directly into severe weather.

It is common practice for aircraft to be inspected following a hailstorm, as the high speed of the falling ice can impact the aircraft and create structural or mechanical damage to the jet that can compromise its flight safety. Hail has the ability to crack or shatter the outer layers of the cockpit windows and could impair pilot visibility and compromise the plane's structural integrity.

Found an error? Send it info@simpleflying.com so it can be corrected.

The nose cone, known as the radome, also houses critical weather radar equipment, and hail can crack, dent, or damage the structure. Lastly, hail entering an engine can damage fan blades or compressors, which, if the engine were running, could lead to internal damage. Following severe hail storms, airlines commonly will order 'aircraft on ground' status until engineers have completed a full safety assessment before clearing the planes to return to regular service.
